headline: Home Minister calls for ACC probe into corruption during interim govt
summary: Salahuddin Ahmed urged the prime minister to investigate all corruption allegations from the 18-month interim government tenure, citing TIB reports.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has urged the prime minister to direct the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) to investigate all allegations of corruption during the 18-month tenure of the interim government.
Speaking during a budget discussion in parliament, the minister stated that those demanding accountability should welcome such a probe to identify where corruption occurred and who was responsible.
The call for investigation follows a recent report by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) which raised allegations of corruption during the interim period.
During the session, Salahuddin also challenged Jamaat-e-Islami lawmakers, questioning the party's role in the 1971 Liberation War and its commitment to Sharia law in its current manifesto.
The minister claimed that Tk 11,000 crore was disbursed under Islami Bank's Rural Development Scheme (RDS) based on political considerations between August 2024 and February 2026.
Addressing the national budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, he stated that the economy was devastated by massive capital flight and institutionalized corruption from previous years.
He cited reports indicating that illicit financial outflows averaged $16 billion annually between 2009 and 2023, totaling Tk 29.25 lakh crore siphoned abroad.
caption:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed wants a full ACC probe into corruption allegations during the interim government's 18-month tenure.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has urged the prime minister to direct the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) to investigate all allegations of corruption during the 18-month tenure of the interim government.

Speaking during a budget discussion in parliament, the minister stated that those demanding accountability should welcome such a probe to identify where corruption occurred and who was responsible.

The call for investigation follows a recent report by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) which raised allegations of corruption during the interim period.

During the session, Salahuddin also challenged Jamaat-e-Islami lawmakers, questioning the party's role in the 1971 Liberation War and its commitment to Sharia law in its current manifesto.

The minister claimed that Tk 11,000 crore was disbursed under Islami Bank's Rural Development Scheme (RDS) based on political considerations between August 2024 and February 2026.

Addressing the national budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, he stated that the economy was devastated by massive capital flight and institutionalized corruption from previous years.

He cited reports indicating that illicit financial outflows averaged $16 billion annually between 2009 and 2023, totaling Tk 29.25 lakh crore siphoned abroad.

headline: Opposition MPs stage walkout in parliament after being denied point of order
summary: Opposition members left the chamber during Sunday's session over disputes regarding bill notices, speaking time, and the denial of a point of order.
details: Opposition MPs staged a walkout at the end of Sunday's parliamentary session after being denied the opportunity to raise a point of order. The tension peaked when Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal invited LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to proceed with a statement despite opposition protests.
caption:
Opposition MPs walk out of parliament! Tensions flare over speaking time and denied points of order.

Opposition MPs staged a walkout at the end of Sunday's parliamentary session after being denied the opportunity to raise a point of order. The tension peaked when Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal invited LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to proceed with a statement despite opposition protests.
